She schemed to swindle her uncle out of his savings.

cards.def: To feel so much excitement, delight, or admiration that you can hardly control yourself.
ex: Teenage fans swoon over the handsome young actor.
His beautiful singing voice made the whole audience swoon.

cards.def: A large tree with broad leaves and smooth bark, common in North America.
ex: A huge sycamore tree shaded the whole front yard.
Birds nested in the branches of a towering sycamore.

cards.def: The small gap where one nerve cell passes signals to another.
ex: Chemical messengers carry the signal as it crosses the synapse.
At a chemical synapse, neurons communicate using tiny molecules.

cards.def: The extra benefit produced when people or things work together, greater than their separate effects.
ex: Combining their skills created synergy across the whole department.
There is clear synergy between the design and marketing teams.

cards.def: To arrange facts or numbers in columns or a table.
ex: The researchers tabulated the results in a clear, simple table.
She neatly tabulated the survey responses by age group.

cards.def: Cheap, showy, and in poor taste.
ex: The hotel lobby was full of tacky plastic decorations.
The bright neon sign made the shop look tacky.

cards.def: A very small amount; a little (used in the phrase 'a tad').
ex: This shirt is a tad too tight across the shoulders.
Add just a tad of salt to balance the sweetness.

cards.def: The young form of a frog or toad, which lives in water and has a tail.
ex: The children love to catch tadpoles in the shallow pond.
Within weeks, a tadpole grows into a small frog.

cards.def: A sharp, curved claw of a bird that hunts, such as an eagle or hawk.
ex: The eagle seized the fish with its sharp talons.
The owl gripped the branch tightly with its talons.

cards.def: A lively ballroom dance from Argentina, performed by two people together.
ex: They learned to dance the tango on their honeymoon.
The café filled with the sound of romantic tango music.

cards.def: Equal in effect to something, usually something bad.
ex: Criticizing the king was once tantamount to treason.
Resigning now would be tantamount to admitting he was guilty.

cards.def: A pattern of crossing colored stripes, traditionally Scottish, or cloth with this pattern.
ex: Her scarf had a bright red and green tartan pattern.
Many Scots proudly wear tartan on special occasions.

cards.def: Having a warm orange-brown color.
ex: The lion's tawny fur blended with the dry grass.
The autumn leaves had turned tawny in color.

cards.def: A hard, yellowish-brown wood from a tropical tree, often used for furniture.
ex: The dining table is made from solid teak.
The garden bench was beautifully made of teak.

cards.def: A small, formal detail in a rule or law that can affect a decision.
ex: The case was dismissed on a legal technicality.
He avoided the fine on a technicality.

cards.def: An expert in science, technology, or management who holds power in government or business.
ex: The new minister is a respected technocrat with years of experience.
For a while the country was ruled by unelected technocrats.

cards.def: The practice of not drinking alcohol.
ex: The temperance movement campaigned against the sale of alcohol.
He practiced temperance and never touched alcohol again.

cards.def: A violent storm with very strong winds.
ex: The small boat was tossed about by a raging tempest.
The sailors were caught in a tempest far from shore.

cards.def: The quality of being very determined and not giving up.
ex: She succeeded through sheer tenacity and hard work.
The team defended their narrow lead with great tenacity.

cards.def: A thin, curling part of a climbing plant that wraps around objects for support.
ex: The vine sent out curling tendrils along the wooden fence.
A thin tendril wraps around the stake for support.

cards.def: the final stop at the end of a railway or bus route; an end point.
ex: The crowded bus terminus was busy during the morning rush.
The old station was once the terminus of the line.

cards.def: A hard, reddish-brown clay used to make pots, tiles, and statues.
ex: Herbs grew in a row of small terracotta pots.
The roof tiles were traditionally made of terracotta.

cards.def: A hormone that controls the development of male sexual features.
ex: Regular exercise can help raise a man's testosterone levels.
Some men take supplements that claim to boost testosterone.

cards.def: Relating to the connection between heat and other forms of energy.
ex: The system slowly reaches thermodynamic equilibrium with its surroundings.
Every engine must obey the basic thermodynamic laws.

cards.def: A horse of a pure breed, especially one bred for racing.
ex: They paid a fortune for a champion thoroughbred racehorse.
The farm has bred thoroughbreds for over fifty years.

cards.def: A main road or public route that people travel along.
ex: The shop sits on a busy thoroughfare in the city center.
Street vendors set up their stalls along the thoroughfare.

cards.def: A period of violent struggle or intense difficulty.
ex: The old empire was clearly in its death throes.
The country is in the throes of a deep recession.

cards.def: A songbird with a brown back and a spotted breast, known for its beautiful song.
ex: A song thrush sang loudly from the top of the hedge.
A thrush built its nest in the old apple tree.

cards.def: To prepare and cultivate land for growing crops.
ex: Farmers till the soil each spring before planting seeds.
The freshly tilled field was ready for the new crop.

cards.def: To make light, high ringing sounds, like a small bell.
ex: The sleigh bells tinkle as the horse trots along.
Glass chimes tinkle in the breeze outside the window.

cards.def: A large, heavy, and usually serious book.
ex: He pulled a weighty tome from the dusty library shelf.
She wrote a massive tome of ancient history.

cards.def: A method of making images of the inside of the body in thin slices.
ex: The hospital used computed tomography to examine the injury.
The doctor ordered a tomography scan of the patient's chest.

cards.def: A clear precious stone, often yellow or blue, used in jewelry.
ex: She wore a ring set with a sparkling blue topaz.
He gave his wife a topaz ring for their anniversary.

cards.def: To move or walk in an unsteady way, as if about to fall.
ex: The injured player slowly tottered to his feet.
The toddler took two steps, then tottered and fell.

cards.def: Easily upset, offended, or annoyed.
ex: She is very touchy about her exam results.
He has been a bit touchy since losing his job.

cards.def: To make someone's hair or something untidy by rubbing or pulling it.
ex: She reached down to tousle the little boy's hair.
The wind gave her a charmingly tousled look.

cards.def: A device that changes one form of energy or signal into another.
ex: A pressure transducer measures the force inside the pipe.
In the sensor, the transducer converts sound into electrical signals.

cards.def: Lying or placed across something, from one side to the other.
ex: A transverse beam supports the roof across the whole room.
The crack ran transverse to the main axis of the bone.

cards.def: To shock and upset someone so severely that it causes lasting emotional harm.
ex: Witnessing such violence can deeply traumatize a child.
The survivors were deeply traumatized by the earthquake.

cards.def: A frame of crossing strips of wood or metal that supports climbing plants.
ex: Roses climbed up the wooden garden trellis by the gate.
The ivy will climb a trellis if you train it.

cards.def: A feeling of fear or worry about something that is going to happen.
ex: He approached the job interview with trepidation.
The soldiers waited for the order with fear and trepidation.

cards.def: To sing or sound with a high, quavering, rapidly repeated note.
ex: At dawn the birds trill from every tree in the garden.
The singer can trill a high note with ease.

cards.def: Having three parts, or involving three groups or countries.
ex: The three nations signed a tripartite agreement on trade.
The report is tripartite in structure, with three clear sections.

cards.def: One of three children born to the same mother at the same time.
ex: The couple were amazed to learn they would have identical triplets.
She gave birth to triplets after a long pregnancy.

cards.def: Small details or facts that are not important.
ex: They chatted about everyday trivia over their morning coffee.
The meeting got bogged down in trivia and achieved nothing.

cards.def: A round fungus that grows underground and is highly valued as a gourmet food.
ex: The chef shaved a black truffle over the fresh pasta.
Trained pigs are used to hunt for truffles in the forest.

cards.def: To make something shorter by cutting off the top or the end.
ex: The system will truncate the text if it is too long.
They released a truncated version of the original report.

cards.def: To move slowly and heavily, especially on wheels.
ex: The old bus trundled along the bumpy country road.
The worker trundled a heavy cart across the yard.

cards.def: A short, thick, rounded underground stem, such as a potato, from which new plants grow.
ex: Each potato tuber can grow into a whole new plant.
Gardeners plant the tubers in early spring.

cards.def: A long piece of cloth wound around the head, worn in some cultures.
ex: Many Sikh men wear a turban every day.
The old man wore a neatly tied white turban.

cards.def: A large bird raised for its meat, especially eaten on holidays.
ex: The family gathered around a golden roast turkey for dinner.
The farm raises turkeys for the holiday season.

cards.def: A very long, pointed tooth that sticks out from the mouth of some animals.
ex: Hunters prized the elephant for its valuable ivory tusks.
The small statue was carved from a walrus tusk.

cards.def: A man's formal black jacket or suit worn on special evening occasions.
ex: The groom decided to wear a tuxedo for the wedding.
He showed up at the dance in a rented tuxedo.

cards.def: A small, thin branch of a tree or bush.
ex: A dry twig snapped under his boot in the quiet forest.
Try not to snap a twig and scare the deer away.

cards.def: A sudden, short, sharp pain.
ex: She felt a twinge as she bent down to tie her shoe.
There was a sharp twinge in his lower back.

cards.def: The style, size, and arrangement of printed letters and text.
ex: The poster used bold typography to grab attention.
She studied the art of typography at design school.

cards.def: A system for sorting things into groups according to their types.
ex: Linguistic typology compares the structures of different languages.
The study proposed a typology of leadership styles.

cards.def: Seeming to be present everywhere at the same time; extremely common.
ex: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern daily life.
The ubiquitous smartphone has changed how we communicate.

cards.def: Relating to the cord that connects an unborn baby to its mother.
ex: The nurse gently clamped the baby's umbilical cord.
The doctor let the father cut the umbilical cord.

cards.def: A situation in which everyone agrees completely about something.
ex: The committee struggled to reach unanimity on the budget.
The vote showed complete unanimity among the members.

cards.def: To do less well than you are able to, or than expected.
ex: Some bright children underachieve at school because they are bored.
Students without support often tend to underachieve.

cards.def: A feeling or tendency that is hidden but can still be sensed.
ex: There was an undercurrent of tension throughout the meeting.
A strong undercurrent of resentment ran through the team.

cards.def: A person or team that is expected to lose a contest or struggle.
ex: Crowds love to root for the underdog in a close match.
The film tells a classic underdog story about a young boxer.

cards.def: To provide too little money for something.
ex: The plan would underfund schools in poorer areas.
The hospital has been chronically underfunded for years.

cards.def: To think that someone or something is less good or important than they really are.
ex: Beginners often underrate the difficulty of learning a language.
He is a badly underrated actor who deserves more praise.

cards.def: To unroll or spread out something that was folded or rolled up.
ex: At dawn the soldiers unfurled a flag over the fort.
The sails unfurl as the crew pulls the ropes.

cards.def: An imaginary animal like a white horse with a single horn on its forehead.
ex: The tapestry showed a mythical unicorn in a green forest.
In the story, the princess learns to ride a unicorn.

cards.def: Difficult to move, carry, or manage because of its size, weight, or complexity.
ex: The old sofa was an unwieldy object to carry upstairs.
The old system became too unwieldy to use efficiently.

cards.def: The process or cost of keeping something in good condition.
ex: The family could no longer afford the upkeep of the estate.
The garden needs regular upkeep to stay beautiful.

cards.def: The final result of a situation.
ex: The upshot of the meeting was a new company policy.
The upshot is that we must cut our spending.

cards.def: To take people's attention away from someone, making yourself seem more important.
ex: He loves to upstage a rival whenever he gets the chance.
The host was upstaged by a surprise celebrity guest.

cards.def: A person who has recently gained wealth or power and behaves arrogantly.
ex: The veteran manager resented the young upstart in the office.
His rivals dismissed him as an upstart with no real experience.

cards.def: a sudden and large increase in something
ex: The store saw a sharp upsurge in demand before the holidays.
Interest in local history is clearly on the upsurge again.

cards.def: an unexpected and unpredictable change or action
ex: Designers must follow the vagaries of fashion each season.
Outdoor events are subject to the vagaries of the weather.

cards.def: a person with no home or steady job who wanders from place to place
ex: A homeless vagrant slept under the bridge near the station.
Years ago he could have been arrested as a vagrant.

cards.def: a person employed to park guests' cars at a hotel or restaurant
ex: The hotel offers free valet parking for dinner guests.
The hotel valet brought our car to the front entrance.

cards.def: great courage, especially in battle or danger
ex: The soldier received a medal for his act of valor.
The firefighters fought the blaze with great valor that night.

cards.def: having patches, streaks, or marks of different colors
ex: The variegated leaves showed streaks of green and creamy white.
The old quilt was richly variegated with scraps of bright fabric.

cards.def: the main team representing a school or college in a sport
ex: She trained all year to make varsity as a freshman.
The varsity coach praised the team after the close win.

cards.def: to sell something, especially in small amounts or to the public
ex: Street traders vend goods from carts along the busy avenue.
Only approved sellers are licensed to vend inside the stadium.

cards.def: to regard someone or something with deep respect
ex: Many cultures venerate their ancestors with yearly ceremonies and offerings.
The nation came to venerate him as a hero after the war.

cards.def: the meat of a deer, eaten as food
ex: We served roast venison with potatoes at the winter dinner.
The butcher recommended a lean cut of venison for the stew.

cards.def: relating to the veins that carry blood back to the heart
ex: Venous blood is darker because it carries less oxygen.
Doctors treated the venous clot in her lower leg quickly.

cards.def: relating to the ventricles, the lower chambers of the heart
ex: The scan showed the ventricular wall was thicker than normal.
Each ventricular contraction pushes blood out to the whole body.

cards.def: a feeling of dizziness and spinning, often caused by an inner-ear problem
ex: She began to suffer from vertigo whenever she looked down.
A sudden bout of vertigo forced him to sit down quickly.

cards.def: a small entrance hall just inside the door of a building
ex: They hung their wet coats in the front vestibule.
Guests were asked to wait in the vestibule until noon.

cards.def: felt or experienced through another person rather than directly
ex: Parents often take vicarious pleasure in their children's small successes.
She lived vicariously through her daughter's success.

cards.def: a person who tries to punish crime personally, without legal authority
ex: A vigilante group began patrolling the neighborhood at night.
Angry residents threatened to take vigilante action against the thieves.

cards.def: a short written description or scene that captures a single moment
ex: The film includes a charming vignette about two old friends.
She painted a vivid vignette of daily life in the port.

cards.def: to say or write cruel and unfair things about someone
ex: The campaign tried to vilify opponents instead of debating ideas.
The coach was unfairly vilified in the press after the loss.

cards.def: a salad dressing made from oil, vinegar, and seasonings
ex: She tossed the greens with a light vinaigrette before serving.
He drizzled vinaigrette over the roasted vegetables and fresh herbs.

cards.def: wanting to hurt someone who has harmed you; spiteful
ex: Beneath his calm manner lay a surprisingly vindictive streak.
She was never vindictive toward the people who doubted her.

cards.def: a type of venomous snake with long, hinged fangs
ex: A venomous viper lay coiled beneath the warm flat rock.
The hiker was bitten by a viper on the rocky trail.

cards.def: having strength and energy traditionally associated with men
ex: He played a virile young man in the war drama.
The horse looked strong and virile as it galloped past.

cards.def: the movable front part of a helmet that protects the eyes and face
ex: The rider lifted his visor to speak with the mechanic.
Her helmet had a tinted visor to block the bright sun.

cards.def: expressing opinions loudly and forcefully
ex: He became a vociferous critic of the new parking rules.
Residents were vociferous in their demands for safer streets.

cards.def: existing or produced in a very large amount
ex: The lawyer arrived carrying voluminous files on the case.
His letters to friends were notoriously voluminous and full of detail.

cards.def: giving rich and pleasurable feelings to the senses
ex: He sank into the sofa with a feeling of voluptuous pleasure.
The dessert was voluptuous and rich, almost too sweet to finish.

cards.def: a religion involving magic and spirits, practiced mainly in Haiti
ex: Some people in the region still practice voodoo today.
The film shows a voodoo ritual with drums and dancing.

cards.def: wanting or consuming very large amounts; extremely eager
ex: The growing teenager had a voracious appetite for junk food.
He read voraciously about history and science.

cards.def: a mass of spinning liquid or air that pulls things toward its center
ex: The storm created a swirling vortex of water near the rocks.
Small boats can be sucked into the vortex below the falls.

cards.def: a person who observes others' pain or private lives without taking part
ex: Through the camera, viewers become voyeurs of a stranger's daily routine.
He accused the press of being voyeurs of other people's suffering.

cards.def: amusingly strange, silly, or unusual
ex: Her wacky sense of humor kept the whole office laughing.
The plan sounded a bit wacky, but it actually succeeded.

cards.def: to walk with short steps, swaying from side to side
ex: The toddler started to waddle like a duck across the room.
She watched the geese waddle down the muddy bank.

cards.def: a very thin, crisp piece of sweet or plain baked food
ex: The dessert came with a thin wafer tucked into the ice cream.
She snapped the wafer in half and shared it with him.

cards.def: done deliberately and cruelly, without a good reason
ex: The war brought wanton destruction to many quiet villages.
The attack seemed wanton and cruel, with no clear purpose.

cards.def: the edge or side of a road or path
ex: Wildflowers grew thickly by the wayside along the quiet lane.
They stopped for the night at a small wayside inn.

cards.def: a small, slender wild animal that hunts mice and other small prey
ex: A wild weasel darted across the path into the hedge.
The children found a weasel's burrow near the old fence.

cards.def: a small, slender sea fish with white flesh, eaten as food.
ex: The chef served a lightly fried fillet of whiting.
We bought some fresh whiting from the harbor market.

cards.def: a soft rushing sound made by fast-moving air or water
ex: The door opened with a loud whoosh of warm air.
We heard the whoosh of the train speeding through the station.

cards.def: thin but strong and tough, especially in body
ex: The climber had a wiry build and remarkable grip strength.
He was small but wiry, and surprisingly hard to beat.

cards.def: (in the past) a public institution where poor people lived and were made to work.
ex: The orphan was sent to the workhouse at a young age.
Conditions in the parish workhouse were harsh and crowded.

cards.def: to take something away with a lot of effort or force
ex: The rebels tried to wrest control of the city from the army.
She fought to wrest the keys from his tight grip.

cards.def: a strong dislike or fear of people from other countries
ex: The crisis led to rising xenophobia in several European cities.
Harsh headlines can fuel xenophobia toward newly arrived immigrants.

cards.def: (historical) a man who owned and farmed a small piece of his own land.
ex: His grandfather was a sturdy yeoman with his own land.
Each yeoman farmer held a few acres near the village.

cards.def: an evergreen tree with dark needles and red berries
ex: An ancient yew tree stood beside the old stone church.
The garden path was lined with neatly clipped yew.

cards.def: unpleasant to taste, smell, or look at (informal)
ex: The medicine tastes yucky, so the children refuse to take it.
The spilled syrup left a yucky mess all over the counter.

cards.def: to destroy or get rid of something quickly, as if with a sudden burst
ex: A good lamp will zap mosquitoes before they reach the patio.
The cream claims to zap away spots and blemishes overnight.

cards.def: a person with very strong beliefs who follows them in an extreme way
ex: The group was led by a religious zealot with rigid rules.
He became such a zealot that he alienated his old friends.

cards.def: the highest or most successful point of something
ex: The empire was at its zenith during that century.
She reached the zenith of her career at forty.

cards.def: a band of the sky divided into twelve signs used in astrology
ex: Leo is a well-known sign of the zodiac.
In the Chinese zodiac, each year is linked to an animal.
